one_line: Zenodo API check of the Gyódi records: the two the scout named carry NO data (record 5233198 'Airbnb and hotels during COVID-19', CC-BY-NC-4.0, one 1.18 MB PDF; record 8135170 spatial-patterns supplement, CC-BY-4.0, one 14.5 MB PDF) — but two sibling Gyódi records DO hold CSVs: 4446043 'Determinants of Airbnb prices in European cities' (Gyódi & Nawaro, CC-BY-4.0, 20 listing-level CSVs, ~10.7 MB, 10 EU cities × weekday/weekend, 2018–19, price/room type/capacity/cleanliness/distance-to-centre/metro/lat-lon + models_robust.py) and 6976622 'Hotel prices' (CC-BY-4.0, 17 CSVs, ~4.7 MB, same 10 cities, summer 2019, hotel-level median 2-person price, stars, hotel-vs-hostel segment, ratings, distance, lat-lon).
abnb_use: Gaps #2 and #9 plus the EMEA ADR read: paired same-city, same-season Airbnb quote prices and hotel prices for Amsterdam, Athens, Barcelona, Berlin, Budapest, Lisbon, London, Paris, Rome, Vienna — a 2018–19 pre-COVID European price level and Airbnb-vs-hotel spread that sits earlier than any Inside Airbnb dump we hold and gives an independent basis check on the EMEA ADR decomposition and the quote-index wedge work.
sample_plan: Keyless direct downloads, ~4.5 MB total (stay under the cap by taking 4 cities from each record, weekday+weekend): `curl -L -o zen4446043_<city>_<days>.csv https://zenodo.org/records/4446043/files/<city>_<days>.csv?download=1` for city in barcelona, paris, london, rome and days in weekdays, weekends (~5.9 MB — drop london_weekends if tight); then `curl -L -o zen6976622_<city>_<days>.csv https://zenodo.org/records/6976622/files/<city>_<days>.csv?download=1` for the same four cities (~3.6 MB). Also grab the 1.18 MB COVID PDF for its nine-city 2018–2020 tables: `curl -L -o gyodi_covid.pdf 'https://zenodo.org/records/5233198/files/Airbnb_Covid_19_Cities__final_-5.pdf?download=1'`. Skip the 14.5 MB ESDA_2023_suplement.pdf. Note Zenodo is currently rate-limiting bots — one file at a time, no parallel fetches.
